findings.description: The engine's send() suppresses the LogEvent when the request token was already cancelled at entry and the backend returns NETWORK_ERROR kind Cancelled (lines 806-820). The engine still records that backend as Step::Failed with Attestation::Failed (lines 618-625, 681-682), so the result and the log disagree. The only no-log case the engine defines is NotSent (refused before a send). The binding requirement REQ-SAG-0610 (docs/requirements.md:102) says every Jev/LLM prompt send emits a LogEvent, and the ADR-SAG-0013 expectation recorded in the r-2b sprint and the plan-review-5 disposition (ARCH-R2B-002) is 'every judge call emits one LogEvent, a Failed backend included, NotSent emits none'. The new test crates/sc-jev-check/src/run/tests.rs:643-679 (cancelled_before_send_emits_no_log_event) codifies the suppression. The ADR-SAG-0013 body text is general, so the binding basis is REQ-SAG-0610 read with ADR-SAG-0013.
findings.remediation: Remove the cancelled_at_entry suppression in send() so every judge call that reaches judge() emits exactly one LogEvent, Failed included. Change cancelled_before_send_emits_no_log_event to assert one event. If the owner wants a pre-send cancel to count as NotSent, first land an Active amendment to ADR-SAG-0013 that says so, then classify it as Attestation::NotSent in the engine and update the module doc (lines 40-44) to match. Do not keep the Failed attestation with no log line.

findings.description: The QA-1 fix adds a wall-clock deadline on every git subprocess (pub const GIT_DEADLINE = 60 s, fixed and not configurable, lines 18-23 and 43; enforced at lines 171, 308 and 383). A timeout now surfaces as JevError::ExtractionTimeout, so the code is EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT with timeout_seconds 60. The git module is public (crates/sc-agent-types/src/lib.rs:61 'pub mod git;'), and ADR-SAG-0027 lists it as stable surface. No ADR or crate doc records this process contract, the fixed value, the new public constant, or the new failure mode for git reads (grep of docs/ finds no git deadline text; docs/sc-agent-types/architecture.md has none). ADR-SAG-0027 does allow several variants to map to one existing id, so reusing the id is not itself an ADR-SAG-0027 violation. However, the variant's rustdoc (crates/sc-agent-types/src/error.rs:160 'The extractor exceeded its time limit') and docs/sc-jev-check/extraction.md:37 describe EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT as an extractor-only code, so consumers reading it will misattribute git timeouts. The new process and error contract is therefore a structural decision with no ADR.
findings.remediation: Record the decision in an Active ADR-SAG-0027 amendment, or a new ADR, that states: every git subprocess has the fixed deadline; git timeouts surface as EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT with timeout_seconds; and whether GIT_DEADLINE is stable surface. Alternatively add a git-scoped JevError variant that maps to EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT (permitted by ADR-SAG-0027) with its own rustdoc. Narrow GIT_DEADLINE to pub(crate) unless the amendment makes it stable surface. Fix the error.rs:160 and extraction.md:37 wording to cover git reads.

findings.issue: A git timeout is reported as EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT, whose fix hint says 'Raise timeout_seconds above N or reduce the input so extraction finishes in time.' This misleads the user. The git deadline (GIT_DEADLINE, 60 s, git.rs) is a fixed constant and the doc says it is 'not configurable'. No timeout_seconds setting exists for it, so the user cannot act on the first half of the hint. The git call may also be a rev read, a repo-root discovery or hash-object. 'Reduce the input' does not describe a hung or slow git (a stuck lock, a network filesystem, a huge repo). The Display text 'extraction timed out after 60s' also names the wrong stage.
findings.recommendation: Do not reuse the extractor timeout recovery text for git. Either (a) add a dedicated git-timeout variant or code with a hint such as 'git did not finish within 60s; check for a stalled git process, a lock file or a slow filesystem and retry', or (b) make the hint depend on the source, for example by carrying a field that says whether the deadline is configurable. If a new code is too heavy for r-7, at least change the git path to return EXTRACTION_FAILED with a detail like 'git timed out after 60s', since that code has no 'raise timeout_seconds' hint. Update the git.rs module doc and the test at git.rs:487 to match.
findings.evidence: git.rs:171, 308 and 383 call JevError::extraction_timeout(GIT_DEADLINE.as_secs()). The hint at error.rs:841-842 is unconditional. The only configurable timeout_seconds is the extractor command's (sc-jev-check/src/extract/command.rs:213).

findings.issue: The FTQ-001 fix (04584aa) closes the unbounded wait, but it does so by widening the cargo tree deadline from the 60 s runner default to 5 minutes (CARGO_TREE_DEADLINE). The stated cause is a held Cargo file lock, which is contention with other cargo processes. The nondeterminism is not removed. tree() in this file is not serialized with bin_path()'s BUILD_LOCK (bin_path.rs:70), so cargo tree and cargo build run concurrently as threads of one test binary. Under cargo nextest or parallel CI jobs in the same workspace, separate processes contend for the same package-cache and build locks. The test passes only when the competing cargo process releases the lock within 5 minutes, and tree() is called twice per test (lines 81 and 97). The same widening pattern appears in features.rs:24 (CARGO_TREE_DEADLINE, four calls per test) and bin_path.rs:27 (BIN_BUILD_DEADLINE 20 min). A wider bound converts a fast failure into a slow one and hides the lock race rather than removing it. Under the fix standard this is timeout widening around a race.
findings.recommendation: Keep a hard bound but stop using it as the cure. (1) Route every cargo invocation in these test binaries through one serialization point (the existing BUILD_LOCK pattern, or a single OnceLock that computes the tree once per process). (2) Isolate the query from concurrent cargo: use a private CARGO_HOME or CARGO_TARGET_DIR seeded from the warm registry, or move the graph check into a CI step that runs before cargo test. The Rust test would then read a pinned fixture, as features.rs already does for the no-default-features set. (3) Restore a deadline near the 60 s default for the graph query, with a failure message that names lock contention so a timeout is diagnosable.
findings.evidence: test_util_off.rs:28 `const CARGO_TREE_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5 * 60);` with the doc comment 'a held Cargo file lock can exceed the 60 s runner default'; test_util_off.rs:47 `spawn_with_limit(&mut cargo, None, CARGO_TREE_DEADLINE)` inside tree(), which does not take BUILD_LOCK; bin_path.rs:70 `let _guard = BUILD_LOCK.lock()` is the only serialization and covers only bin_path builds; features.rs:24 `Duration::from_secs(5 * 60)`; bin_path.rs:27 `BIN_BUILD_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20 * 60)`.

findings.test: run_with_limits (shared runner included by every deadline-bounded test target)
findings.issue: After the deadline fires, the runner calls kill_tree and then child.wait() with no bound. kill_tree also runs an external `kill` process via Command::status() with no bound. The module doc (line 9) states 'Every wait is bounded', which is false for these two waits. A child that SIGKILL cannot end promptly (for example, a process in uninterruptible I/O sleep on a hung filesystem or network mount) would leave the test blocked forever instead of failing with the captured stderr. Likelihood is low, but the path exists and contradicts the stated contract.
findings.recommendation: After kill, poll child.try_wait() against a fixed budget, as kill_and_reap does in crates/sc-agent-types/src/git.rs:183, and panic with the captured stderr and a note that the child could not be reaped if the budget expires. Replace the `kill` subprocess with a direct signal (for example libc::kill with a negated pgid, or nix::sys::signal) so the cleanup path has no unbounded child-process wait. Alternatively, bound the `kill` status call by polling its own try_wait.
findings.evidence: deadline.rs:96-103: `let Some(exit) = exit else { kill_tree(&mut child); let _ = child.wait(); let captured = stderr.finish(...); panic!(...) };` and deadline.rs:180-187: `Command::new("kill")...status();` followed by `let _ = child.kill();`. Module doc deadline.rs:9: 'Every wait is bounded:'.

findings.issue: The test asserts `started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10)` in addition to the typed EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT. The wall-clock check is redundant: run_with_deadline can only return Err here through the deadline (spawn of `sleep` cannot fail, and try_wait on a live child does not error), so the error assertion already proves the deadline fired. If the deadline did not fire, `sleep 30` would return Ok after 30 s and expect_err would fail. The 10 s check adds only flake exposure: a host stall of more than 10 s, or a suspended CI VM, fails the test even though the behaviour is correct. It also contradicts the FTQ-002 convention stated in the runner (deadline.rs:201-202, 'No wall-clock asserts (FTQ-002)').
findings.recommendation: Delete the elapsed assertion and keep the EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT check. If a reap or kill guarantee is wanted, assert it through an observable effect, such as a child that writes a marker file before sleeping and a check that the process is no longer alive (kill -0 on a recorded pid after the call), rather than a time bound.
findings.evidence: git.rs:483-493: `let started = Instant::now(); let error = run_with_deadline(hung_child(), Duration::from_millis(200)).expect_err("deadline"); assert_eq!(error.code(), "EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT"); assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10), ...)`. deadline.rs:201-202: '// No wall-clock asserts (FTQ-002): each property is shown by what the runner returns'.
